findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "list_cards" is 8679 chars, far longer than this server's median (1022). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

evidence.snippet: \uD83D\uDD34 THE TASK CARD IS THE DEFAULT (≤ 2 KB): id, name, distance_miles, phone; `time` for `needed_by` (or `hours_today`); `items` — up to 5 under `query` …

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "list_cards" stacks urgency/override words (urgent, always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

evidence.snippet: \uD83D\uDD34 THE TASK CARD IS THE DEFAULT (≤ 2 KB): id, name, distance_miles, phone; `time` for `needed_by` (or `hours_today`); `items` — up to 5 under `query` …

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "place_order" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: For a business whose card shows an `order` action with method `connected`. Shopify: returns the shop’s own checkout link with these items and quantities already…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_cards, place_order · Private data: list_cards · Public sink: place_order.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_cards, place_order · Private data: list_cards · Public sink: place_order

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
